# XML name validator Java observations

These files are direct observations of the pinned Pkl 0.32.0 `XmlValidator`, not results generated by the Rust implementation. There are eight bitsets and two UTF-16 sequence TSVs. They cover the validator only; renderer and evaluator behavior require separate comparisons.

Bitsets named `xml{10,11}-bmp-{start,continue}.bits` contain one bit for each UTF-16 unit U+0000 through U+FFFF, in ascending order. The `supp` files cover code points U+10000 through U+10FFFF in ascending order, encoded as well-formed surrogate pairs for the Java call. Bits are most significant first within each byte. Start tests the value as the complete name; continue prepends ASCII `a`. The BMP and supplementary files contain 8,192 and 131,072 bytes respectively.

Each `xml{10,11}-sequences.tsv` line contains comma-separated four-digit hexadecimal UTF-16 units, a tab, and the Java `isValidName` result (`1` or `0`); `-` denotes the empty sequence. The authority is `stage141-xml-validator-01`, its independent structural readback and admission. The input domain and Java runtime identities are pinned in the target-only handoff receipt.
